title: Question: stream isolation guidance for an embedded Arti client carrying both Nostr relay and Zcash light-wallet traffic on mobile
description:
Hello,

I am building Shielded Mesh, a fork of bitchat (iOS and Android) that embeds Arti in-process, as bitchat already does. I am not seeking funding, press or users. Please relabel or close this if a question is not appropriate for the tracker.

The app sends two kinds of traffic over Arti: Nostr relay websockets, and Zcash light-wallet sync (gRPC to lightwalletd servers). I want to stop an exit or a server from linking a user's messaging identity to their wallet activity through shared circuits.

Questions:

1. Is it the recommended Arti API pattern to use separate isolation groups (IsolationToken or equivalent) for each traffic class, and possibly per Nostr identity?
2. Are there known costs or pitfalls with keeping several isolated long-lived streams open on mobile (battery, circuit build limits, background suspension on iOS)?

Full design note available on request.

Thank you,
Rita, Planetary Perspective

title: tor-dirmgr's rusqlite <0.40.0 upper bound blocks embedding arti-client alongside other rusqlite-0.40+ dependents
description:
tor-dirmgr (pulled in transitively by arti-client via onion-service-client/onion-service-service, and more generally by any use of directory management) requires rusqlite >=0.36.0, <0.40.0. Because rusqlite declares links = "sqlite3", Cargo forbids two different rusqlite versions coexisting anywhere in one workspace's unified dependency graph — so any application that wants to use arti-client alongside a different crate requiring rusqlite ^0.40 (e.g. for a newer SQLCipher/OpenSSL feature) cannot build at all, with no feature flag available to opt out of the rusqlite dependency in tor-dirmgr.

Would it be possible to widen the upper bound (e.g. to <0.41.0 or whatever range covers current 0.4x releases), assuming there's no known incompatibility with 0.40+? This would let arti-client compose more easily with other crates in the current Rust SQLite ecosystem.

```

```

The principal complaint here is, as the error seems to have been nonfatal, there's no way for the calling code (onionmasq) to know what it is; the bootstrapping code simply loops forever without ever actually returning an error. In this case, it was evidently due to the state directory being corrupted after the unclean shutdown somehow, since clearing the cache instantly fixed it (which would be a bug in its own right, if I had any actual details of the problem).

Would it be possible to provide some mechanism to allow embedding code to have more control or insight into the bootstrap retry process? This is really quite a problem in the Tor VPN use case, since this failure just manifests itself to the user as an indefinite failure to make progress (it does at least set the 'stuck' flag, but we really would prefer the actual error object).

(Yes, I know I can configure it to give up after n attempts, etc -- but then the only error received is an overly generic `CantAdvanceState`).
